sections.skill: Plan charitable giving, research charities, and understand the tax treatment of donations

questions.prompt: Nia wants to give 5% of her $2,400 monthly take-home pay to charity. How much is that each month?
questions.intro: Many people plan giving as part of their budget, often as a percent of income. Giving time (volunteering) and skills also counts.
sources: IRS (Tax Exempt Organization Search): Lists organizations eligible to receive tax-deductible charitable contributions. (https://apps.irs.gov/app/eos/)

IRS (Charitable contributions): Charitable contributions are generally deductible only for taxpayers who itemize deductions, and only to qualified organizations; rules can change by tax year. (https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/charitable-organizations/charitable-contribution-deductions)

New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs (Charities Registration): Most charities that solicit in New Jersey must register with the state, and residents can look up registration status. (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/charities/)

FTC (Donating wisely): Research charities before giving, be wary of pressure and payment by gift card or wire, and watch for scams after disasters. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/donating-wisely-avoiding-charity-scams)

questions.prompt: Before donating to a charity she has never heard of, what should Nia check?

choices.text: Its registration and how it uses money
Only the emotional story told in its ad
How fast the caller wants payment

questions.correct_answer: Its registration and how it uses money
questions.intro: Research charities with the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search, the charity's own reports, and charity evaluators. In New Jersey, most charities that ask for donations must register with the Division of Consumer Affairs.
questions.feedback: Confirm the charity is real and see how it spends donations.

questions.prompt: Nia takes the standard deduction. Can she generally deduct her $1,440 of yearly donations on her federal return?

choices.text: Yes; every donation is fully deductible for everyone
Yes; she gets the $1,440 back as a refund
No; donations are taxed as income

questions.intro: Charitable donations to qualified organizations are generally deductible only for taxpayers who itemize. A deduction lowers taxable income; it is not a dollar-for-dollar refund. Rules can change by tax year.
questions.feedback: With the standard deduction, donations generally are not deducted separately.
